इन्द्रजाल: Indrajāla nt.: Name of a missile. (1) One of the missiles used by Arjuna against the Gandharvas accompanying Citra-sena; they were burnt by these arrows 3. 234. 17-18; (2) one of the अस्त्रस् used by Dhṛtarāṣṭra's sons against Yudhiṣṭhira for covering him up with arrows 8. 43. 21 [In both these references Indrajāla is mentioned with Sthūṇākarṇa]; (3) Arjuna released shower of arrows against the Sindhu warriors; the arrows formed a net which looked like the one produced by the Indrajāla weapon (? or which looked like the effect of some magic ? तद् इन्द्रजालप्रतिमं बाणजालम् अमित्रहा । व्यसृजत्) 14. 76. 31.
इन्द्रास्त्र: Indrāstra nt.: Name of a missile. Used by Arjuna 3. 168. 2. [See Ain-drāstra].
इषीका: Iṣīkā f.: A reed or a straw, instead of an arrow, used as a missile by Aśvat-thāman; the अस्त्र employed on it not named, but apparently identical with Brahmaśiras (10. 12. 4, 40). Described as a ‘powerful missile’ (परमास्त्र) 10. 13. 17; 10. 15. 12, 23, 33; 10. 16. 8; ‘heavenly’ (दिव्य) 10. 15. 16, 25; ‘unparalleled’ (दुरासद) 10. 15. 16; ‘fierce’ (घोर) 10. 15. 11; ‘unfailing’ (अमोघ) 10. 15. 31; (10. 16. 8); ‘produc-ing big flames and surrounded by a circle of lustre’ (महाज्वालं तेजोमण्डलसं-वृतम्) 10. 14. 8; when challenged by Bhīma, who was followed by Arjuna and Yudhiṣṭhira in a chariot, driven by Kṛṣṇa, Aśvatthāman took a reed (इषीका) in the left hand (सवेय्न पाणिना) and thought of the heavenly missile, recited मन्त्रस् on it to imbibe it with the lustre of fire (वह्नितेजो ऽनुमन्त्र्य वै 10. 15. 16), and released it for the destruction of the Pāṇḍavas (अपाण्ड-वाय 10. 13. 18; 10. 15. 16); fire broke out from the reed which threatened to burn the three worlds 10. 13. 15-20; to counter it, Arjuna released Brahmaśiras (10. 15. 23) saying ‘let the missile be pacified by missile’ (अस्त्रम् अस्त्रेण शाम्यताम्) 10. 14. 2-6; 10. 15. 20; (however, according to 1. 1. 155 Arjuna said ‘स्वस्ति’ while releasing his missile); apprehending great danger to the creatures from the fire released by the two missiles, Nārada and Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana stood between them and appealed to the two heroes to withdraw their missiles since they were never used by any one before 10. 14. 7-16; accordingly, Arjuna withdrew it (10. 15. 1, 5, 10), but Aśvatthāman could not withdraw it (10. 15. 11) and he admitted to the sages his inability to follow their advice 10. 15. 15; he said the missile must achieve its purpose and destroy all the sons of Pāṇḍu 10. 15. 17; but Vyāsa pointed out that if Aśvat-thāman's परमास्त्र were to subdue Arjuna's Brahmaśiras there would be no rain in the land for twelve years; (however, according to 1. 1. 155 one अस्त्र was pacified by the other अस्त्रम् अस्त्रेण शान्तम्); Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana therefore asked again Aśvatthāman to with-draw his missile and save the nation and the Pāṇḍavas 10. 15. 25-26; but since the missile could not be totally withdrawn, Aśvatthāman suggested that the missile should fall, not on the Pāṇḍavas, but on their foetus (इषीका निपतिष्यति । गर्भेषु पाण्डवेयानाम् 10. 15. 31); when permitted by Vyāsa to do that, Aśvatthāman directed the missile to the foetus 10. 15. 32-33; it was then destined to hit the foetus in the womb of Uttarā 10. 16. 7-8 [See Aiṣikāstra and Brahmaśiras].
इन्द्रलोकाभिगमन: Indralokābhigamana nt.: Name of the 32nd पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha 1. 2. 43, 30, 70. Alluded to in the contents of the Āraṇya-kaparvan (दर्शनं लोकपालानां स्वर्गा-रोहणम् एव च 1. 2. 107; it comprises the अध्यायस् 3. 43-49; 79.
इन्द्रविजय: Indravijaya, Śakravijaya, Vijaya nt.: Name of an आख्यान 5. 18. 19 or उपाख्यान 5. 18. 16; also called Śakravijaya (उपा-ख्यानम् इदं शक्रविजयम्) 5. 18. 16, or Vijaya (for short) 5. 18. 17. It comprises अध्यायस् 5. 9-18; described as an incident that occurred in the past, an ancient इतिहास (पुरा वृत्तम् इतिहासं पुरा-तनम्) 5. 9. 2; comparable to the Veda (in importance) (वेदसंमितम्) 5. 18. 16; it should be heard by a king desiring victory when his army and that of his enemy are arrayed (for a battle) 5. 18. 16; that is why Śalya narrated the आख्यान Vijaya, in which Indra's victory over Vṛtra and the downfall of Nahuṣa were described, to Yudhiṣṭhira before the start of the war 5. 18. 17; one who diligently (नियतः) recites this Indravijaya Ākhyāna is washed of all his sins, wins heaven, and rejoices in this as well as in the next world; he has no danger from the enemy, and is never without a son (i. e. he does not lose his sons in war ? न चारिजं भयं तस्य न चापुत्रो भवेन् नरः); he does not meet with adversity and gets long life; he is victorious in all battles and never knows defeat 5. 18. 19-20.
इक्षुमती: Ikṣumatī f.: Name of a river. Situated near the Kurukṣetra; along this river lived the Nāga Takṣaka and his son Aśvasena (कुरुक्षेत्रे निवसतां नदीम् इक्षुमतीम् अनु) 1. 3. 145; finds place in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-vaṃśa 13. 151. 20, 2.
इक्षुमालिनी: Ikṣumālinī f.: Name of a river. One of the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa enumerated by Saṃjaya 6. 10. 16, 5; its water used by people for drinking 6. 10. 13.
इक्षुवर्धनिका: Ikṣuvardhanikā f.: Name of a river. One of the rivers of the Śākadvīpa enumerated by Saṃjaya 6. 12. 30; all these excellent rivers are holy (पुण्यास् ता हि सरिद्-वराः) 6. 12. 32.
इन्द्रकील: Indrakīla m.: Name of a mountain. Arjuna, after crossing the Himavant and the Gandhamādana mountains, reached Indrakīla where he saw Indra in the form of an ascetic 3. 38. 30.
इन्द्रतीर्थ: Indratīrtha nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। A. Location: Not far from the आश्रम of Srucāvatī, daughter of Bharadvāja, near the तीर्थ Badarapācana 9. 47. 17. B. Description: excellent (उत्तम) 9. 47. 17; famous in the three worlds (त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुते) 9. 47. 17; auspicious (शिव) 9. 48. 5; holy (पुण्य), most ancient (सनातन), which frees one of all sins (सर्वपाप-प्रमोचन) 9. 48. 5. C. Name: Since Indra performed there a hundred sacrifices, the तीर्थ came to be known after him (तत्र ह्य् अमरराजो ऽसाव् ईजे क्रतुशतेन ह … तस्य नाम्ना च तत् तीर्थम् … इन्द्रतीर्थम् इति ख्यातम्) 9. 48. 2, 5. D. Events: (i) Epic: Balarāma, in his तीर्थयात्रा, went from the Badarapācanatīrtha to Indra-tīrtha; he took bath according to the rites and gave riches and jewels to Brāhmaṇas 9. 48. 1; Balarāma bathed there (उपस्पृश्य) according to the rites and honoured Brāh-maṇas by giving them drinks, clothes and food (पानाच्छादनभोजनैः); from there he went to the Rāmatīrtha 9. 48. 6; (ii) Mytho-logical: Indra performed there, without any hindrance, a hundred sacrifices according to the prescribed rites, rich in meat, and giving all kinds of दक्षिणास् (निरर्गलान् सजारू-थ्यान् सर्वान् विविधदक्षिणान्; Nī. on Bom. Ed. 9. 49. 1: जारूथ्यान् पुष्टान्) with the help of priests versed in the Vedas; in those sacrifices he gave ample wealth to Bṛhaspati 9. 48. 2-3; (iii) Indra, after his meeting with Srucāvatī, went to the nearby Indra-tīrtha and began to mutter मन्त्रस् (ततो जप्यं जजाप सः) 9. 47. 17.
इन्द्रतोया: Indratoyā f.: Name of a river. Near the Gandhamādana mountain; if one who is controlled and pure bathes there and fasts for three nights he gets the fruit of a horse sacrifice 13. 26. 11.
इन्द्रद्युम्न: Indradyumna nt.: Name of a lake. A. Location: Pāṇḍu, with his two wives, after crossing the Himavant mountain proceeded to the Gandhamādana, and after reaching the Indradyumna lake and crossing the Haṃsakūṭa, he lived as an ascetic on the Śataśṛṅga mountain 1. 110. 45; the lake was situated beyond the mountain Himavant (mentioned in 3. 191. 4), the dwelling place of the long-lived crane called Nādījaṅgha 3. 191. 9-10; a tortoise, Akūpāra by name and older than Prākārakarṇa, also lived in this lake 3. 191. 14, 18. B. Origin: Akūpāra told his visitors on the bank of this lake (3. 191. 16) that the lake was created by the treading of the cows given as gifts by the king Indradyumna in the sacrifices per-formed by him at that place (सरश् चेदम् अस्य दक्षिणादत्ताभिर् गोभिर् अतिक्रम-माणाभिः कृतम्) 3. 191. 18.
इन्द्रपर्वत: Indraparvata m.: Name of a mountain. When Bhīma was in the country of the Videhas, he conquered the seven chiefs of the Kirātas in the neighbourhood of the Indra-parvata mountain (इन्द्रपर्वतम् अन्तिकात्) 2. 27. 13.
इन्द्रमार्ग: Indramārga m.: Name of a तीर्थ। Benefits of visiting this तीर्थ: (1) One who is on a pilgrimage (तीर्थसेवी), if he fasts for a day and night at the Indramārga he is glorified in the Śakraloka (शक्रलोके महीयते) 3. 81. 158; (2) By bathing at Indramārga one is awakened in a विमान, praised by the Apsarases (विबोध्यते विमान-स्थः सो ऽप्सरोभिर् अभिष्टुतः) 13. 26. 9; (3) If one gives offerings to manes at this तीर्थ (इन्द्रमार्गे च तर्पयन्) he enjoys सुधा in his next life (सुधां वै लभते भोक्तुं यो नरो जायते पुनः) 13. 26. 15.
इन्द्रस्य: Indrasya prasravaṇam nt.: Name of a cascade. A. Location: Located on an excellent, auspicious mountain which was visited by persons of friendly and upright disposition (मैत्राणाम् ऋजुबुद्धीनाम् अयं गिरिवरः शुभः) 3. 125. 21. B. Description: Holy (पुण्य) 3. 125. 20. C. Mytho-logical event: Here Dhātṛ, Vidhātṛ and Varuṇa became composed and lived a highly virtuous life; from here they ascended to heaven (?) (यत्र धाता विधाता च वरुणश् चोर्ध्वम् आगताः । इह ते न्यवसन् राजन् क्षान्ताः परमधर्मिणः) 3. 125. 20-21.
इरामा: Irāmā f.: Name of a river. One of the rivers seen by Mārkaṇḍeya in the belly of the child (Bāla 3. 186. 83 i. e. Nārāyaṇa 3. 187. 3) 3. 186. 95.
इरावती: Irāvatī f.: Name of a river. A. Location: Enumerated among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa whose water was used by people for drinking 6. 10. 15, 5, 13; the country where the five rivers, among which one is Irāvatī, with the Sindhu as the sixth flow that is known as the Āraṭṭas (आरट्टा नाम ते देशाः) 8. 30. 35-36; the Bāhlīka country lies beyond the rivers Śatadruka and the Irāvatī rivers 8. 30. 21. B. Description: Excellent river (सरिद्-वराः) 13. 134. 14; सरितां वराः) 13. 134. 19. C. Characteristics: (1) There are forests of Pīlu trees on this river (यत्र पीलुवनान्य् अपि) 8. 30. 35-36; (2) Irāvatī and other rivers contain water of all the तीर्थस् (सर्वतीर्थोदकैर् युताः) 13. 134. 12; (3) Meeting the ocean (सागरगमाः) 13. 134. 14. D. Importance: (1) One of the rivers which wait upon Śiva for his bath (उपस्परशनहेतोस् त्वा समीपस्था उपासते) 13. 134. 12; (2) These rivers, Sarasvatī, Irāvatī and others, were expert in what constitutes the duties of women (स्त्रीधर्मकुशलाः); therefore Umā wanted to consult them on स्त्रीधर्म before ex-pounding it to Śiva (तं (स्त्रीधर्मं) तु संमन्त्र्य युष्माभिर् वक्तुम् इच्छामि शङ्करे) 13. 134. 16, 19-20, 13; Umā thus wants to honour them 13. 134. 12, 21; (3) One of the rivers which wait upon Varuṇa in his सभा 2. 9. 19. E. Event: Bhoja, Gopati and Tālaketu were killed by Kṛṣṇa on the banks of Irāvatī 3. 13. 30.
इलास्पद: Ilāspada nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Situated near the Saraka तीर्थ; by bathing there and by worshipping (अर्चयित्वा) gods and manes, one does not meet with calamity and wins the fruit of the Vājapeya sacrifice 3. 81. 63-64.
इन्द्रप्रस्थ: Indraprastha nt.: Name of a city, the capital of the Pāṇḍavas; earlier called Khāṇ-ḍavaprastha; occasionally referred to also as Śakraprastha (1. 213. 57; 2. 25. 20; 16. 8. 10, 11, 68; 17. 1. 9), Śatakratuprastha (3. 24. 11), Śakrapura (5. 30. 47); desig-nated variously as पुर (1. 199. 27; 3. 24. 11, also पुरोत्तम and पुरश्रेष्ठ see below Description), नगर (1. 55. 25; 1. 199. 28, 39; 1. 213. 57), राष्ट्र 1. 199. 47 (besides प्रस्थ as in its name). A. Location: Near the river Yamunā (व्यचरद् यमुनाकूले पार्थेन सह) 1. 213. 57; (गच्छामो यमुनां प्रति) 1. 214. 14. B. Description: Delightful (रम्य) 1. 213. 57; best city (पुरोत्तम) 1. 199. 33; 1. 213. 22; 2. 25. 20; 2. 65. 17; (पुरश्रेष्ठ) 1. 199. 30, 49; unrivalled (अप्रतिम) 3. 24. 11; large (महन्त्) 1. 199. 47; 3. 24. 11; looking like the city of gods (देवपुरप्र-काश) 3. 24. 11; city of the righteous people (पुण्यजनोपेत) 1. 199. 47; it had well distributed large roads (सुविभक्तमहा-पथ) 1. 55. 24; full of clean people and adorned by merchants (सुसंमृष्टजना-कीर्णं वणिग्भिर् उपशोभितम्) 1. 213. 33, full of communities (जनपदोपेत) 1. 55. 24; (also see the next section). C. Found-ing of the city: Dhṛtarāṣṭra gave half of the Kuru kingdom to the Pāṇḍavas and asked them to settle down at Khāṇḍava-prastha (अर्धं राज्यस्य संप्राप्य खा-ण्डवप्रस्थम् आविश); the Pāṇḍavas had to pass through a dense forest to reach Khāṇḍavaprastha from Hāstinapura (प्र-तस्थिरे ततो घोरं वनं तत् … खाण्डव-प्रस्थम् आविशन्) 1. 199. 25-26; led by Kṛṣṇa, the Pāṇḍavas renovated the city so that it looked like heaven (कृष्णपुरो-गमाः । मण्डयां चक्रिरे तद् वै पुरं स्वर्गवत्) 1. 199. 27; they performed शान्ति on a holy and auspicious spot and then measured out the town under the guidance of Vyāsa (ततः पुण्ये शिवे देशे शान्तिं कृत्वा महारथाः । नगरं मापयाम् आसुर् द्वैपायनपुरोगमाः) 1. 199. 28; 3. 24. 11; its protective deep and tall walls, wide gates, tall गोपुरस्, different weapons stored in it, and its palatial buildings des-cribed in 1. 199. 29-36; it had gardens all around filled with trees of different kinds and birds (विविधैर् द्रुमैः । … नानाद्विज-गणायुतम्; the trees are listed); the gar-dens were filled with the notes of excited peacocks and cuckoos (मत्तबर्हिणसं-घुष्टं कोकिलैश् च सदामदैः) 1. 199. 39-43; it had clean, residential houses, creeper houses (लतागृह), houses display-ing pictures on their walls (चित्रगृह) and artificial mountains for the sport of kings (जगतिपर्वत; Nī. who reads अजगतिपर्-वतैः (Bom. Ed. 1. 207. 46) says: नृप-लीलायात्रार्थैः कृत्रिमैः पर्वतैः) 1. 199. 44; it had ponds (वापी) filled with water, lakes (सरस्), fragrant with lotuses and adorned with swans, कारण्डव and चक्र-वाक birds, varied and delightful lotus ponds covered with clusters of lotus plants (रम्याश् च विविधास् तत्र पुष्करिण्यो वना-वृताः), and other beautiful ponds, large and wide (तडागानि च रम्याणि बृहन्ति च म-हान्ति च) 1. 199. 44-46; Brāhmaṇas learned in all the Vedas came to settle down there, as also men who knew different languages (सर्वभाषाविदस् तथा), merchants from all directions seeking to make money (वणिजश् चाभ्ययुस् तत्र देशे दिग्भ्यो ध-नार्थिनः), and artisans who were skilled in different crafts (सर्वशिल्पविदश् चैव वासायाभ्यगमंस् तदा) 1. 199. 37-38; Indraprastha, shining with its various white, excellent palatial buildings, shone like heaven (विरोचमानं विविधैः पाण्डुरैर् भवनो-त्तमैः ॥ तत् त्रिविष्टपसंकाशम् इन्द्र-प्रस्थं व्यरोचत । ) 1. 199. 34-35; there Yudhiṣṭhira had his residence on a beauti-ful, auspicious spot; filled with wealth it shone like the residence of Kubera (तत्र रम्ये शुभे देशे कौरव्यस्य निवेशनम् । शुशुभे धनसंपूर्णं धनाध्यक्ष-क्षयोपमम्) 1. 199. 36; the Pāṇḍavas, as they settled down there, developed a liking for the town (तेषां … राष्ट्रम् आवसतां … पाण्डवानां … शश्वत् प्रीतिर् अवर्धत) 1. 199. 47; the excellent town, with those five Indra-like archers, shone like Bhogavatī with the Nāgas (शुशुभे तत् पुरश्रेष्ठं नागैर् भोगवती यथा) 1. 199. 49; the Pāṇḍavas thus became the inhabitants of Khāṇḍava-prastha (समपद्यन्त खाण्डवप्रस्थवा-सिनः) 1. 199. 48; they thus got the kingdom of Indraprastha (एवं संप्राप्य राज्यं तद् इन्द्रप्रस्थे) 1. 200. 1; Pāṇḍavas' settl-ing down at Khāṇḍavaprastha and ruling from there half of the (Kuru) kingdom is referred to in the Parvasaṃgrahaparvan (खाण्डवप्रस्थवासश् च तथा राज्यार्ध-शासनम्) 1. 2. 89; also mentioned briefly in the summary of the Mahābhārata (अस्मा-भिः खाण्डवप्रस्थे युष्मद्वासो ऽनुचिन्ति-तः) 1. 55. 23-27; while describing the Pāṇḍavas' rule at Indraprastha Draupadī told Satyabhāmā that a hundred thousand horses and ten अयुतस् of elephants were in regular attendance of Yudhiṣṭhira (शतम् अश्वसहस्राणि दशनागायुतानि च । युधि-ष्ठिरस्यानुयात्रम् इन्द्रप्रस्थनिवासिनः) 3. 222. 48 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 233. 50; अनुयात्रं स्वैरयात्रायाम् अपि परिवार-भूतम्); Pāṇḍavas' going to Khāṇḍava-prastha alluded to by Draupadī when she introduced herself to Koṭikāśya 3. 250. 5; Draupadī, while lamenting over the condi-tion of the Pāṇḍavas during their stay in the Virāṭanagara remembered Yudhiṣṭhira's glory while living in Indraprastha 4. 17. 15-21, 23-26, 28. D. Epic events: (1) When the cows of a Brāhmaṇa were stolen by thieves he came to Khāṇḍavaprastha and blamed the Pāṇḍavas 1. 205. 6; (2) While ruling from Indraprastha the Pāṇḍa-vas subjugated other kings at the instance of Dhṛtarāṣṭra and Bhīṣma (apparently even before the Rājasūya) (इन्द्रप्रस्थे वसन्तस् ते जघ्नुर् अन्यान् नराधिपान् । शासनाद् धृतराष्ट्रस्य राज्ञः शान्तनवस्य च ॥ ) 1. 214. 1; (3) Dharmarāja, who was at Indpraprastha, was informed of Arjuna's plan to abduct Subhadrā and his permi-ssion was obtained 1. 211. 25; (4) Arjuna, along with Subhadrā, returned to Khāṇḍava-prastha when he completed his period of exile of twelve years 1. 213. 13, 22; (5) The Yādavas went to Khāṇḍavaprastha to offer marriage gifts to Arjuna 1. 213. 29; (this is referred to in the Anukramaṇīparvan 1. 1. 103); when Kṛṣṇa, Balarāma and other Yādavas arrived, the city of Khāṇḍava-prastha was gaily decorated with flags and banners, its roads were swept and sprink-led with water, flowers scattered all around, cool and fragrant sandalwood juice was abundantly used, and fragrant अगुरु burnt at every place (विवेश खाण्डवप्रस्थं पताकाध्वजशोभितम् । सिक्तसंमृष्टपन्-थानं पुष्पप्रकरशोभितम् । चन्दनस्य रसैः शीतैः पुण्यगन्धैर् निषेवितम् ॥ दह्यतागुरुणा चैव देशे देशे सुगन्धिना) 1. 213. 31-33; (6) When the Yādavas left, after giving gifts to Arjuna, Kṛṣṇa stayed behind at Śakraprastha (उवास नगरे रम्ये श्रक्रप्रस्थे महामनाः) 1. 213. 57; (7) Sairandhrī told Uttara that Bṛhannaḍā was the charioteer of Arjuna when he defeated all kinds of beings at Khāṇḍavaprastha (अजयत् खाण्डव-प्रस्थे) 4. 34. 15 (here Khāṇḍavaprastha stands for Khāṇḍava forest); this feat of Arjuna at Khāṇḍavaprastha (= Khāṇḍava forest) also referred to by Kṛṣṇa in his address to Duryodhana (अजयत् खाण्डव-प्रस्थे) 5. 122. 52, and by Karṇa when he spoke to Śalya (प्रस्थे ऽजयत् खाण्डवे सव्यसाची) 8. 29. 18; (8) After a com-fortable stay (सुखवास) at Khāṇḍava-prastha Kṛṣṇa wished to leave for Dvārakā 2. 2. 1; (9) Kṛṣṇa went again to Indra-prastha when invited by Yudhiṣṭhira for consultation regarding his wish to perform a Rājasūya 2. 12. 30-31; (10) After the death of Jarāsandha, Kṛṣṇa returned to Indraprastha with Bhīma and Arjuna 2. 22. 44; (11) When the four younger Pāṇḍavas went for the conquest of the four directions before the Rājasūya, Yudhi-ṣṭhira stayed back at Khāṇḍavaprastha 2. 30. 10; (12) After completing successfully his expedition to the north Arjuna return-ed to Śakraprastha with all kinds of tributes (शक्रप्रस्थं पुरोत्तमम्) 2. 25. 20; (13) When Bhīma returned to Indraprastha after his expedition to the east he reported to Yudhiṣṭhira the great wealth brought by him 2. 27. 28; (14) Nakula went to the west from Khāṇḍava-prastha 2. 29. 2; when he came back to Yudhiṣṭhira at Indraprastha he too report-ed to him the wealth brought by him 2. 29. 18; (15) After the Rājasūya, when Dur-yodhana visited the Mayasabhā in Indra-prastha, the Pāṇḍavas laughed at Duryo-dhana (Bhīṣma told this to Yudhiṣṭhira) 12. 124. 5 (reference to 2. 43. 7, 9); (16) Dhṛtarāṣṭra asked Vidura to go to Khāṇ-ḍavaprastha to invite Yudhiṣṭhira for a game of dice 2. 45. 56; (17) At the end of the first game of dice, Dhṛtarāṣṭra per-mitted Yudhiṣṭhira to return to Khāṇḍva-prastha 2. 65. 15; accordingly Yudhiṣṭhira, with his brothers and Draupadī, left for Indraprastha 2. 65. 17; (18) The bright prosperity (at the time of Rājasūya) of Yudhiṣṭhira while he was ruling at Indrapra-stha (इन्द्रप्रस्थगते … युधिष्ठिरे) was snatched away from him by Duryodhana in the game of dice (Karṇa told Duryodhana) 3. 226. 5-6; (19) People lamented when Yudhiṣṭhira had to leave for the forest leaving behind the great city Śatakratu-prastha founded by himself (स्वयं निवेश्य  … पुरं महत् … शतक्रतुप्रस्थम् … हित्वा प्रयातः क्व नु धर्मराजः) 3. 24. 11; (20) Kṛṣṇa had assured Yudhiṣṭhira when he met him in the forest that he (Kṛṣṇa) could kill the Kauravas and get back for him his prosperity which he had seen at Indraprastha at the time of Rāja-sūya (and of which he was now deprived) 3. 48. 17, 23; (21) Duryodhana re-minded Dhṛtarāṣṭra that when Kṛṣṇa and the other kings met the Pāṇḍavas in the forest, at a place not far from Indraprastha (वनं प्रव्राजितान् पार्थान् … इन्द्रप्रस्थ-स्य चादूरात् समाजग्मुः), they blamed Dhṛtarāṣṭra and the other Kauravas 5. 54. 2, 4; (22) Aśvatthāman asked Karṇa in derision in which battle did he (Karṇa) win Indraprastha from the Pāṇḍavas; now Karṇa should fight with Arjuna (at the time of the cow raid at Virāṭanagara) since he was responsible for the game of dice and for winning Indraprastha 4. 45. 10, 21; (23) Yudhiṣṭhira told Saṃjaya “Let Suyodhana recognize my kingship at Indraprastha and I shall be at peace with the Kauravas” (शान्तिं गमिष्यामि यथा त्वम् आत्थ । इन्द्र-प्रस्थे भवतु ममैव राज्यं सुयोधनो यच्छतु भारताग्र्यः ॥ ) 5. 26. 28; he again asked Saṃjaya to tell Duryodhana: “Hand over Śakrapura to me or get ready for battle” (ददस्व वा शक्रपुरं ममैव युध्यस्व वा भारतमुख्य वीर ॥ ) 5. 30. 47; Bhīṣma, after he fell on the battlefield, also advised to hand over half of the kingdom to the Pāṇḍavas and let Yudhiṣṭhira rule at Indraprastha (रा-ज्यस्यार्धं दीयतां पाण्डवानाम् इन्द्र-प्रस्थं धर्मराजो ऽनुशास्तु) 6. 116; 48. (24) Kṛṣṇa reminded Dhṛtarāṣṭra that he himself and his sons had sent away Yudhi-ṣṭhira to Indraprastha (इन्द्रप्रस्थं त्व-यैवासौ सपुत्रेण विवासितः), where he (Yudhiṣṭhira) brought under control other kings and made them subservient to Dhṛta-rāṣṭra 5. 93. 55-56 (reference to 1. 199. 24-25; 1. 214. 1); (25) After the Pāṇḍa-vas won the war, Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna rejoic-ed at Indraprastha 14. 15. 5; (26) Arjuna told Vasudeva that he would take with him women folk, as also the young and the old, of the Vṛṣṇis, to Indraprastha 16. 8. 5; He told the Brāhmaṇas and the merchants of Dvārakā (नैगमाः), who had gathered around him, that he would take with him the Vṛṣṇis and the Andhakas to Śakraprastha since Dvārakā would be merged in the ocean (शक्र-प्रस्थम् अहं नेष्ये वृष्ण्यन्धकजनं स्वयम् । इदं तु नगरं सर्वं समुद्रः प्लावयिष्यति) 16. 8. 10; he also told them that Vajra would be their king at Śakra-prastha (वज्रो ऽयं भवतां राजा शक्र-प्रस्थे भवीष्यति) 16. 8. 11; Arjuna reha-bilitated the old, the young and the women of the Vṛṣṇis and the Andhakas at Śakra-prastha (शक्रप्रस्थे न्यवेशयत्) 16. 8. 68; Arjuna gave the kingdom of Indra-prastha to Vajra 16. 8. 70; (27) Yudhi-ṣṭhira told Subhadrā, when he decided to abandon the kingdom, that Parikṣit would be the king of Hāstinapura and Vajra, the Yādava, of Śakraprastha (परिक्षिद् धास्तिन-पुरे शक्रप्रस्थे तु यादवः । वज्रो राजा) 17. 1. 9. E. Similes: (1) Khāṇḍavaprastha compared with Bhogavatī, the city of the Nāgas (सुशुभे तत् पुरश्रेष्ठं नागैर् भोगवती यथा) 1. 1. 9. 30; 1. 199. 49; (2) Compared with heaven (तत् त्रिविष्टपसं-काशं इन्द्रप्रस्थं व्यरोचत) 1. 199. 35; (देवपुरप्रकाशम्) 3. 24. 11. [See Uda-yendu]
इक्ष्वाकु: Ikṣvāku m. (sg. and pl.): Designation of kings born in the line of king Ikṣvāku; the lineage is often referred to as Ikṣvāku-kula or Ikṣvākuvaṃśa. A. Description: High-souled (महा-त्मन्) 3. 195. 34; very virtuous among kings (नृपतिसत्तम) 1. 164. 11. B. Seat of their kingdom: Ayodhyā (अयोध्यायाम् इक्ष्वाकुकुलोत्पन्नः … परिक्षित्) 3. 190. 3; (गच्छ … अयोध्यां नगरीम् … ॥ स … राजा … । इक्ष्वाकुकुलजः … मित्रं चैव भविष्यति) 3. 63. 19-20. C. Past history: (1) Kṛṣṇa told Yudhiṣṭhira that the Kṣatri-yas of bygone days claimed their lineage either from Aila or from Ikṣvāku; hence they were either Ailavaṃśyas or Ikṣvākus; together they formed a hundred and one families (यद् इदं क्षत्रसंज्ञितम् … ऐलस्येक्ष्वाकुवंशस्य प्रकृतिं परिच-क्षते । … ऐलवंश्याश् तु ये राजंस् तथेइ-वेक्ष्वाकवो नृपाः । तानि चैकशतं विद्धि कुलानि भरतर्षभ ॥ ) 2. 13. 2, 4-5; (2) Gandharva Aṅgāraparṇa told Arjuna that the Ikṣvāku kings, having obtained Vasiṣṭha as their Purohita, obtained the rulership of earth; with Vasiṣṭha as their Purohita they offered many sacrifices (यं प्राप्य … नराधिपाः । इक्ष्वाकवो महीपाला लेभिरे पृथिवीम् इमां ॥ पुरोहितवरं प्राप्य वसिष्ठम् ऋषिसत्तमम् । ईजिरे क्र-तुभिश् चापि नृपास् ते … ॥ स हि तान् याजयाम् आस सर्वान् नृपतिसत्तमान्) 1. 164. 9-11; (3) The line of Ikṣvāku was continued by Dṛḍhāśva, Kapilāśva and Candrāśva, the three sons of Kuvalāśva (तेभ्यः परम्-परा राजन्न् इक्ष्वाकूणाम् महात्मनाम्) 3. 195. 34. D. The family is referred to as Ikṣvākuvaṃśa, Ikṣvākukula, Aikṣvāka (-kī fem.), or just Ikṣvāku: (1) King Yuvanāśva (इक्ष्वाकुवंशप्रभवः) 3. 126. 5; (2) Kalmāṣapāda (इक्ष्वाकुवंशजः) 1. 166. 1; (3) Saudāsa Mitrasaha (इक्ष्वाकुवंशजः) 13. 77. 1; (4) Aja (इक्ष्वाकुवंशजः) 3. 258. 6; (5) Parikṣit (इक्ष्वाकुकुलोत्पन्नः) 3. 190. 3; (6) Ṛtuparṇa (इक्ष्वाकुकुलजः) 3. 63. 20; (7) Sagara (इक्ष्वाकूणां कुले जातः) 3. 104. 6; (ऐक्ष्वाकम्) 12. 129. 122; (8) A princess (not named), wife of Suhotra (ऐक्ष्वाकी) 1. 89. 26; (9) Triśaṅku (इक्ष्वाकुः) 13. 3. 9; (10) Bhagīratha (इक्ष्वाकुम्) 12. 29. 62; (11) Haryaśva (इक्ष्वाकुम्) 5. 113. 18; (12) Kuvalāśva (इक्ष्वाकुः) 3. 192. 4, 7; (13) Subala (इक्ष्वाकुराज्ञः) 3. 249. 8; (14) Rāma (इक्ष्वाकुनन्दनम्) 3. 273. 8; (°नन्दनः) 3. 275. 8; (इक्ष्वाकुः) 3. 267. 35; (15) Lakṣmaṇa (इक्ष्वाकुनन्दनः) 3. 274. 10; (16) Suvarṇā, wife of Suhotra and mother of Hastin (इक्ष्वाकुकन्याम्) 1. 90. 36. E. Epic event: Arjuna killed in battle principal Ikṣvāku heroes who happened to come within the range of his arrows (इक्ष्वाकुमुख्यांश् च … जघानातिरथः संख्ये बाणगोचरम् आगतान्) 3. 255. 28. F. Past events: (1) Rāma told the ocean, who appeared to him in dream, that he was an Ikṣvāku and his (ocean's) kinsman (इक्ष्वाकुर् अस्मि ते ज्ञातिर् इति रामस् तम् अब्रवीत्) 3. 267. 35; (2) Kal-māṣapāda asked a boon from Vasiṣṭha, viz. that he (V.) might be pleased to beget a son on his (K.'s) wife, so that he might pay back the debt to Ikṣvākus and for the continuation of the line of Ikṣvākus (इक्ष्वा-कूणां तु येनाहम् अनृणः स्यां द्विजो-त्तम । … इक्ष्वाकुकुलवृद्धये) 1. 168. 11-12; (3) King Śala (son of Parikṣit), said that even though Ikṣvākus, Dala and his other subjects obeyed his order, he would not give back Vāmya horses to Vāmadeva (इक्ष्वाकवो यदि ब्रह्मन् दलो वा विधेया मे यदि वान्ये विशो ऽपि । नोत्स्रक्ष्ये ऽहं वामदेवस्य वाम्यौ) 3. 190. 68; (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 192. 58: (विधेयाआज्ञाकारिणः); when Śala was killed, the Ikṣvākus anointed Dala, his younger brother, as king (ततो विदित्वा नृपतिं निपातितम् इक्ष्वाकवो वै दलम् अभ्यषिञ्चन्) 3. 190. 69; King Dala addressed his kinsmen as Ikṣvākus; he asked them to bring for him another sharp arrow (anointed with poison) with which he would kill Vāmadeva and do a feat dear to them (इक्ष्वाकवो हन्त चरामि वः प्रियं … आनीयताम् अपरस् तिग्मतेजाः (सायकः)) 3. 190. 75; king Dala again addressed his kinsmen as Ikṣvākus and pointed out to them that he was checked (by Vāmadeva) and was unable to release the arrow (इक्ष्वाकवः पश्यत मां गृही-तं न वै शक्नोम्य् एष शरं विमोक्तुम्) 3. 190. 77; Vāmadeva told Dala's wife that she had saved the royal family and that she should rule her subjects and the large kingdom of Ikṣvākus (त्वया त्रातं राज-कुलं शुभेक्षणे … प्रशाधीमं स्वज-नं राजपुत्रि इक्ष्वाकुराज्यं सुमहच् चाप्य् अनिन्द्ये ॥ ) 3. 190. 80.
इन्द्रवत्स: Indravatsa m. (pl.): Name of a people. Indravatsas mentioned among those eighteen peoples whose kings extirpated their kinsmen, friends and relatives; king Dhāraṇa extirpated the Indravatsas (अष्टा-दशेमे राजानः … ये समुच्चिच्छिदुर् ज्ञातीन् सुहृदश् च सबान्धवान् ॥ … धारणश् चेन्द्रवत्सानाम् समुच्छेत्ता) 5. 72. 11, 16.
इलावृत: Ilāvṛta m.: Name of a Varṣa. Ilāvṛta stands in the middle of the form of a bow of which two Varṣas (viz. Airā-vata and Bhārata) stand on the northern and southern ends; there are in all five Varṣas between Airāvata varṣa and Bhārata varṣa (धनुःसंस्थे महाराज द्वे वर्षे दक्षिणोत्तरे । इलावृतं मध्यमं तु पञ्च वर्षाणि चैव ह । ) 6. 7. 36; cf. 6. 7. 6, 35.
